Jedit charged him. The two went over the rail together and fell eighteen metres to the sand. The fall nearly killed the tiger. Johan, wrapped in his protections, got up dazed and unhurt, with the battle as good as won.
The sand opened under him, as it had opened under Jaeger Ojanen, and a wurm swallowed the Emperor of the Northern Realms.

When word of Johan's death spread, his generals turned on one another. The fleet fled north into the mountains so fast that it left its foot soldiers behind in the jungle of Efrava. They surrendered over the next few days in exchange for their lives, and their supplies fed the tiger warriors for months. Hazezon took pity on the prisoners and escorted them home to Tirras.

A long peace followed in Jamuraa. Jedit Ojanen became the leader of the Robaran Mercenaries. The mercenaries spread out and explored distant islands in Adira's name and founded colonies there. Hazezon governed Bryce for ten more years. Then he sailed away at the head of a fleet of flying ships. His flagship was named Adira's Kite. It is said to have wandered to the far ends of the world, giving gold and magic to the innocent and bringing down tyrants with armies of warriors made of sand.

Jedit lived to head a whole dynasty of children and grandchildren. Under his leadership all the tiger tribes were reunited. They went back to Scarwood, rebuilt the Tabernacle, and founded an empire that took its place among the peoples of Dominaria. The cat warriors, who had hidden in a desert for seven centuries, were free to roam the world.

One other event of these years belongs to no chapter of its own. It took place on Shandalar, the small, wandering, mana-soaked plane where the soul of the necromancer Lim-Dûl lies shut in the Chain Veil. His imprisoned soul powers the Great Barrier, the wall that keeps outside planeswalkers away from Shandalar. The plane is protected by an immortal mage called the Guardian, and its magic is taught by five guilds, each under a guildlord.

The magical uproar of Shandalar's earlier wars had spread out through the Multiverse like ripples. A planeswalker named Arzakon traced the ripples to their source and was astonished at how much power lay there. About 3346 AR Arzakon tried to force a way in. The Guardian strengthened the Barrier and threw the intruder back with ease.

So Arzakon tried corruption. The planeswalker reached the five guildlords and told them of a great Spell of Dominion, which would give them the mastery of all Shandalar. In truth the spell would do one thing. It would seek out the Chain Veil and destroy it, and the Barrier would fall. The guildlords believed what they were told. They turned on the Guardian and killed his body. One of the five was the lich Skavius Slan, who was the walking corpse of the Guardian's old fellow pupil.

The Guardian's spirit survived. It found a wandering amateur spellcaster, somebody of no reputation at all, and warned and trained that person. The newcomer hunted down the five guildlords one at a time and beat every one of them before they could gather what the spell required. By then the Barrier had weakened just enough for Arzakon to break through. The planeswalker fought the unknown spellcaster and lost, and was cast out of Shandalar for a very long time. The spellcaster's name is not recorded. This was the plot of a computer game, and the hero was whoever was playing it.

chapters.title: The Mana Rig, the Forest and the Skyship
sources: MTG Wiki, "Time Streams" (the novel by J. Robert King, 1999)

blocks.p: The last chapter told of Urza's school on the island of Tolaria. Urza is the ancient planeswalker who is preparing Dominaria for an invasion from Phyrexia, the plane of flesh and machine. At the school he is known as Master Malzra. His partner is the wizard Barrin.

In 3307 AR Urza's attempt to build a time machine destroyed the first Academy and left Tolaria broken into regions where time runs fast or slow. A Phyrexian spy named K'rrik and his followers were trapped in a gorge of fast time, where ten years pass for every year outside. There K'rrik breeds generation after generation of negators, which are Phyrexia's bred killers.

Three people around Urza matter in what follows. Karn is the golem of silver whom Urza built as a time traveller and gave a mind by setting in him the heart of his dead friend Xantcha. Jhoira is an artificer from the volcanic land of Shiv, who survived alone on the ruined island for ten years and no longer ages. Teferi is a brilliant young mage from Zhalfir, whom Jhoira freed from a bubble of slow time in 3330 AR.
By 3330 AR the Academy was rebuilt, and the gorge was still there.
Urza did not want to send people into the gorge to die. He decided to send machines.

He spent years building them: mechanical falcons with edges like razors, hundreds of them, made to seek out Phyrexian flesh and tear it apart. In 3337 AR he loosed them into the gorge. The day is remembered as the Day of Falcons.

The falcons killed more than half of the Phyrexians. Then they were overcome. Urza himself was caught and dragged down into the fast time. Any mortal would have died. Urza lived, because he was a planeswalker, and K'rrik took him prisoner. K'rrik knew that a planeswalker escapes by concentrating, and he made sure that Urza could not concentrate. He had him cut open, again and again, without pause.

Karn saw his maker fall and went in after him. The silver golem fought his way down through the negators, found Urza and carried him out. Barrin flew in above the gorge in an ornithopter, the flapping-winged flying machine of the Brothers' War, to cover their escape.

Urza was not grateful to himself. He had gone in to destroy the enemy, and he had left hundreds of machines behind. K'rrik's one shortage had been metal. Now he had metal and powerstones, and for every year that Tolaria spent preparing, he would have ten.

From then on it was open war on the island. About 3345 AR there was a sad small accident of a different kind. A monster of illusion that Barrin had summoned by mistake killed a student named Skaven before Urza could dispel it. The Academy was a dangerous place even without Phyrexians.
In 3347 AR Urza left the defence of the island to Barrin and went to Shiv.

Shiv is a continent of volcanoes, where the sea near the coast comes close to boiling. Jhoira's people, the nomad Ghitu, live there. So do goblins, and the viashino, who are a people of upright lizards, and the great red dragons for which the land is famous.

Urza had noticed something that Jhoira wore: an amulet made of a metal that he recognised. It was Thran metal, an almost indestructible alloy whose making had been lost for five thousand years. He went to find where it came from.

On a cliff in the Shivan desert stood a structure of metal the size of a small city. The Thran had built it as a factory. It was called the Mana Rig, and its purpose was to make powerstones, the crystals that drive machines, and to forge Thran metal. It had stood idle since the Thran fell. The goblins whose ancestors had been its slaves had forgotten what it was for and made a religion of it, and the viashino held it sacred too. When Urza walked into it he very nearly started a war.

He made a peace instead. The viashino were being attacked by a dragon, Gherridarigaaz. She was angry because her son, a young dragon named Rhammidarigaaz, had chosen to be the champion of the viashino and live among them. Urza faced the mother down and made her leave the viashino alone. In return they let him use the Rig. He then persuaded the goblins and the viashino to work it together. That was necessary, because the Thran had built parts of it for goblin-sized workers.
He brought Jhoira and Teferi from Tolaria to run it. The two worked side by side there for years, and something more than friendship grew between them at last.
The Rig began to turn out what Urza needed: Thran metal, powerstones, and a set of extraordinary devices. Urza called the whole collection the Legacy.

The Legacy was Urza's answer to Yawgmoth, and it was a strange one. It was a group of artifacts, each powerful by itself, designed so that when all of them were brought together they would form a single weapon, far greater than its parts. That weapon would be able to kill Yawgmoth himself.
Then he saw the gap in his own plan. A weapon needs someone to wield it. The Legacy needed an heir: a mortal champion, strong and good enough to carry it and to lead the peoples of Dominaria.

No such person existed. So Urza set out to make one. Shortly after 3347 AR he began what was called the Bloodline project. He would quietly arrange marriages, over many generations, among the families of Dominaria with the strongest natural gifts, so that those gifts grew with each generation until the hero he needed was born. It meant treating people as breeding stock, without their knowledge, for centuries. It troubled Barrin deeply, and it split the Academy.
Karn, too, was counted as part of the Legacy from the beginning, though nobody told him what that would mean.

Urza had designed the centrepiece of the Legacy. It was a ship that could fly, and that could do something no machine had ever done: cross from one plane to another without a planeswalker to carry it. With such a ship, mortals could strike at Phyrexian targets anywhere.

Its frame would be Thran metal. Its hull had to be wood, and no ordinary wood would do. It had to be alive. Urza knew of only one place to find such a thing, the forest of Yavimaya. In 3352 AR he went there alone. Barrin warned him that Tolaria's defences needed strengthening before he went anywhere. Urza waved the warning away.
Yavimaya was the forest that the refugees of Argoth had settled three thousand years earlier. Argoth was the island that Urza had destroyed, with everything on it, when he set off the Sylex.
The forest was aware, and it had a voice. Its guardian spirit was named Multani. He was a being of the same kind as Titania, the guardian of Argoth, who had died in Urza's blast.

Multani received the visitor coldly. Urza apologised. It was not enough. The forest closed round him and sealed him inside the trunk of an ancient tree. There Multani made him feel, as his own, all the pain that he had inflicted on Argoth: every tree, every creature, and the long death of Titania.
It went on for years. The chronicle says five, and the summary of the novel says three.

parts.h: The invasion of Tolaria (3347 to 3357 AR)

blocks.p: While Urza hung in the tree, K'rrik's creatures were coming out of the gorge. The first attacks began in 3347 AR. They grew larger every year. For ten years Barrin and the Academy beat them back, killing negators by the hundred.

In 3357 AR the gorge emptied itself onto the island: an army of monsters and warped half-human things. They broke the walls and poured into the school. Barrin called up every artifact creature Tolaria possessed and prepared to die with his students. Before the end he sent out a magical call for help, aimed at Urza.
The call reached the tree. It carried the sight of the students being slaughtered. That did what years of pain had not done, and Urza tore himself free.
Multani tried to hold him and was caught up in the planeswalker's power, and so the spirit of Yavimaya was carried along, inside Urza, a passenger in his mind.

Urza arrived in the middle of the battle. He sealed breaches with molten stone and burned the attackers down. He was determined that there would not be a second Argoth. He told Barrin that the fight could only be ended by killing K'rrik. Then he went to Shiv and came back with an army: Jhoira and Teferi, Shivan warriors, machines of Thran metal, goblins, viashino, the young dragon Rhammidarigaaz, and Karn. It was not enough. He went back once more and persuaded the mother dragon Gherridarigaaz to come, by promising to bring her together again with her son. Her fire turned the battle in the courtyard.

Urza went for the gorge alone. He broke a dam above it and rode the flood down into the fast time. He found the breeding vaults, rows of vats in which half-formed Phyrexians were growing, fed on what had been taken from the bodies of the dead. He destroyed them with lightning, and the effort drained him.

Then one of his own falcons, captured twenty years before and rebuilt to hunt Urza himself, tore into him. It kept wounding him faster than he could heal, and he could not gather himself to walk away. K'rrik came to finish him. The spy took his time over it. He told Urza that there were hidden chambers holding thousands more warriors, ready to come out and overrun the world.

Multani had watched all of it from inside Urza's mind. He had seen Urza fight to protect every living thing on the island. He had now seen Phyrexia. The spirit of the forest gave his strength to the man who had burned Argoth.
It was enough for one step between places. Urza used it to step inside K'rrik's body. The Phyrexian burst apart.
Multani then woke the forests of Tolaria themselves against the remaining negators, and with his guidance Urza cleaned out the last chambers. The invasion of Tolaria was over.

Multani had made up his mind. Phyrexia was a danger to every forest and every living thing, and only Urza could deal with it. He forgave nothing, and he became Urza's ally. Yavimaya began to arm itself against the invasion to come.
He also gave Urza what he had come for. It was a seed from the heart of Yavimaya, called the Weatherseed. From it a living hull could be grown.
It was during these battles that the students of Tolaria finally learned who old Master Malzra was.

The ship still lacked its heart. To cross between planes it needed a powerstone holding an almost unthinkable amount of mana, about as much as a whole world contains. To get that, Urza would have to drain a plane.
He knew of one that was dying anyway, and it was dying because of him.

Serra's Realm was the small heaven of floating islands and angels where the planeswalker Serra had healed him, two and a half thousand years earlier. Phyrexia's hunters had followed his trail there. Their presence had poisoned the place. Serra had left in grief, and a made plane decays without its maker. She had left her chief angel, Radiant, to rule.

Urza went to see what could be saved. Radiant received him with reproaches, which were deserved. She let him watch her armies at work. They were purifying the Realm of Phyrexians. They carried torches that glowed yellow when Phyrexians were near. Urza watched the torches glow and the soldiers kill, and he knew that the people they were killing were not Phyrexians at all. They were ordinary frightened villagers. Radiant called them dissidents.
Urza offered to take the refugees away with him, together with any spies hidden among them. Radiant refused, and declared that Urza was a Phyrexian himself.

The truth was worse than she could see. Her own minister of war, Gorig, was a Phyrexian sleeper agent. The torches did not detect anything. They drained white mana out of the people they were turned on. That mana flowed to Gorig, who turned it into black mana for Phyrexia. Radiant was proud and quick to judge, and she had been led into butchering her own people in a holy war against an enemy who stood at her elbow. And the Realm was made of white mana. Every angel and every villager who died brought the whole plane nearer to collapse.
Urza came back again and again and carried out refugees a few hundred at a time. It was far too slow.
In 3360 AR the ship was finished. Urza named it the Weatherlight. He made Jhoira its captain and Karn its master of engines.

The Weatherlight sailed out of Dominaria into Serra's Realm, loaded with artifact soldiers, with Urza riding the dragon Gherridarigaaz and Barrin riding her son beside it. They found the plane on the edge of falling in.

The angels attacked at once. Every angel the crew killed hastened the end, and they had no choice. Gorig came at the ship in a monstrous form. Barrin fought him and was nearly beaten, and in fighting him understood that Gorig himself was the store of all the stolen mana. With a last desperate spell of command, Barrin tricked the creature into impaling itself on the ship. The mana in him poured into the Weatherlight's powerstone.

Radiant challenged Urza to single combat in the sky. She hurled a spell at him that would have killed him. Gherridarigaaz threw herself into its path and died. Urza attacked the archangel in a rage, and she proved the stronger. She tore the Mightstone and the Weakstone out of his skull.

She carried the two stones, and the dying planeswalker, to the palace that had been Serra's. There she tried to join them together. She did not know what those stones were. They were the two halves of the great powerstone of Koilos.

The blast destroyed the palace. In the last instant Radiant understood what she had done to her Realm, and cried out that she was the mad one. Then she was gone, and the stones were back in Urza's head, and he was whole again.

The Weatherlight took the last refugees aboard, thousands of them. As Serra's Realm folded in on itself, Urza drew the energy of the whole dying plane into the ship's powerstone. Jhoira steered the Weatherlight out as the heaven behind it ceased to exist.
The ship now carried a world's worth of power. It could travel between planes by itself, with no planeswalker aboard.

Jhoira took the people of Serra's Realm to Zhalfir, Teferi's homeland, where they were given a place to live. Teferi had gone home to serve as a royal mage and was trying to end a civil war there. He asked Jhoira to marry him. She declined, kindly. She went back to Shiv to run the Mana Rig, and Karn missed her badly.

Barrin, looking back on those years, thought that Urza was sane at last. He had faced what he did at Argoth and had been punished for it. He had begun to have friends, where before he had only had companions.

Sanity did not make him gentle. The Bloodline project went on. And about 3370 AR Urza began its second part. One hero would not be enough. He needed an army. He had an agent named Riand steal the egg of a sea dragon to get what he needed, and he began to grow soldiers in vats. They were tall, blue-skinned and sexless, bred to obey and to fight Phyrexians and to do nothing else. He named them the Metathran, in honour of the Thran. Several researchers left the Academy in disgust. Urza stored his soldiers asleep in bubbles of time, by the thousand, against the day they would be needed.

chapters.title: The Bloodlines and the Making of Rath
sources: MTG Wiki, "Bloodlines" (the novel by Loren L. Coleman, 1999)

blocks.p: Urza, the ancient planeswalker, is preparing Dominaria for an invasion from Phyrexia. By 3370 AR he had three things in hand.

The first was the Legacy, a collection of artifacts designed to combine into one weapon able to kill Yawgmoth, the lord of Phyrexia. Its centrepiece was the Weatherlight, a flying ship that could cross between planes. Karn, the golem of silver with the heart of Urza's dead friend Xantcha, was part of it too.
The second was his school on the island of Tolaria, run with the wizard Barrin. The island's broken time let its researchers do decades of work in a year and live for centuries.

The third was a plan to breed a hero. The Legacy needed a mortal to wield it. Urza had begun to arrange marriages in secret among Dominaria's most gifted families, generation after generation, so as to produce that person. This was the Bloodline project. He had also begun to grow an army of blue-skinned soldiers in vats, the Metathran.

This chapter covers nearly five hundred years, in which both sides built. Its main source is the novel Bloodlines by Loren L. Coleman, as the encyclopaedia reports it. The novel gives its events only broad spans of years, and those are used here.

parts.h: The project in the open (3385 to 3571 AR)

blocks.p: For some decades the Bloodline project was known only to Urza and a few others. From about 3385 AR he revealed it to the Academy, and from then on most of Tolaria worked on it.

Dozens of families were chosen. Urza looked above all to the continent of Jamuraa and to a region called the Domains, where the land was rich in white mana, the magic of order and healing, and where there were old lines of warriors. Through influence and careful planning the Academy came to decide, almost completely, who in those families married whom. Often a child's future partner was chosen on the day the child was born. The families did not know.

The work was led by Barrin and by a woman named Rayne. Rayne had come to the Academy as a scholar, older than students usually were, and had risen fast to be a tutor and then chancellor, the head of the school in the founders' absence. She often opposed Urza's plans outright. Barrin fell in love with her and married her.

Barrin did not know one thing about that. Urza had promoted Rayne partly for her ability and partly because she herself was a product of his bloodlines. He had seen what a child of hers and Barrin's might be, and he had put the two of them in each other's way on purpose. Urza bred his closest friend like the rest.

The project divided the school. Barrin argued with Urza openly. When the Metathran were made, some researchers resigned in protest. That had a bad effect. Those who stayed were the ones with fewer scruples, and there were fewer people left to watch them.
Jhoira had left Tolaria to run the Mana Rig in Shiv, and Karn missed her terribly. He sank deeper and deeper into a black despair that was slowly consuming him. Barrin saw it and begged Urza to help.
Urza's help was drastic. He set a limit inside Karn's mind. From then on the golem could remember only the last twenty years of his life. Everything older faded.
There was one thing Karn refused to lose. Every night he took out a picture of Jhoira and said the same words over to himself: Jhoira is my friend.

Yawgmoth had not forgotten the planeswalker who blasted a hole in his world. In these same years he woke one of the great lords of his inner circle, a Phyrexian named Croag, and gave him two tasks. He was to find Urza and kill him. And he was to prepare the invasion.
The first task Croag pursued in the old way, with negators, the killers bred to hunt. He sent pack after pack of them on Urza's trail.
The second task was something new.
Yawgmoth wanted to put his armies onto Dominaria directly. For that he created a second artificial plane, named Rath.

Rath was hidden in a small pocket of space attached to Dominaria itself, where planeswalkers would have difficulty finding it. At its centre stood a vast machine called the Hub. The Hub poured out a substance called flowstone. Flowstone is a kind of living rock, dimly aware, which can be commanded to take any shape, and the whole of Rath was made of it. The machine never stopped, and so the plane grew. It was meant to go on growing for centuries, until it was exactly as large as Dominaria. On that day Rath would be laid over Dominaria, the one world settling into the same place as the other, and every army standing on Rath would at that moment be standing on Dominaria. That event was called the overlay.
Inside the Hub was a fortress, the Stronghold, slung across the crater of a volcano three miles high. From there the plane was governed, in Phyrexia's name, by a ruler with the title of evincar.

Rath had peoples of its own, and none of them had come willingly. As the plane grew, patches of it briefly overlapped patches of Dominaria, and whoever stood there was carried across. Croag also took people on purpose. Three human peoples lived on Rath, the Kor, the Vec and the Dal. There were elves in a forest called Skyshroud and merfolk in the waters beneath it. They scraped a living under rulers who regarded them as a nuisance, and they rebelled again and again.

Croag found his governor in a village on Dominaria called Coracin. Its elder was a man named Davvol, who was dying of an illness. His own people had turned away from him when he fell sick and at last drove him out. Croag came to the village looking for an ancient machine kept in its vault. Davvol told him how to get in.

Croag took him to Rath. Davvol was put in charge of building the plane, of crushing its rebels, and of killing Urza. So that he would not die, the Phyrexians replaced parts of his body with machinery. He hated what was left of his flesh, which reminded him of his disease, and he longed to be rid of it altogether. He set about breeding better negators.

Davvol also carried out Croag's experiments in moving things between worlds: sending troops from Rath out across the Multiverse and bringing pieces of Dominaria in. Those experiments had victims. Some of the peoples being moved were caught halfway and stuck there, in the emptiness between Rath and Dominaria, unable to touch either. They became half-real beings of shadow.

The forest of Yavimaya was now Urza's ally, and it had to be made ready for war. An elf named Rofellos was sent there from Llanowar, a great elven forest on another continent with a fierce warrior tradition. He was to teach Yavimaya to defend itself.

Rofellos took the place of the forest's own guardian spirit, Multani, as the voice of Yavimaya, and Multani went abroad to see the world. Under the elf's guidance the forest and everything in it grew warlike. When Multani came home he hardly recognised it. A forest cannot have two minds. Yavimaya had to choose, and Rofellos, who had found it more than he could bear to be the voice of a living forest, stepped aside. Multani, grateful all the same, offered to teach him the magic of his own kind.

One of the researchers who stayed on the Bloodline project was a brilliant man named Gatha. He thought that Barrin's scruples were holding the work back. In secret he began to do what was forbidden. He bred human stock mixed with Phyrexian flesh.
He was found out and expelled. He took his work north, to Keld.

Keld is the nation of warriors founded by Kradak in the Ice Age, a hard land whose people are larger and stronger than other humans and whose magic is fire. The Keldons despised the soft little foreigner. A powerful Keldon lord protected him, and Gatha went to work on Keldon blood.

His results came much faster than Urza's and were much more dangerous. The warriors he made stirred a lust for battle in the troops around them, and drew strength from that lust in turn, so that the frenzy fed itself. The Keldons called the greatest of them witch kings.
Urza's own slower work went on. In those two centuries he drew into it a family of Benalia.

Benalia is the nation that rose in the Domains when the Sheoltun Empire fell. It is ruled by seven noble clans. One of them, Clan Capashen, traced its descent from the old Sheoltun nobility. Urza went to its leader, Nathan Capashen, with an offer. If a certain cousin of his, Jaffry, married a certain woman named Myrr, the clan would have fifty years of service from a golem of silver. Nathan agreed. So Karn went to live among the Capashens, and the bloodline that mattered most was placed under his care.

Generation followed generation. Not every branch came to anything. One Capashen of great power, Gavvan, proved to be a dead end. His line could grow no stronger, and it was judged unfit to carry the Legacy. The line that led on ran through his sister Therri, a messenger and warrior.
In Jamuraa a second family was being shaped in the same way. Its last daughter would be a sea captain named Sisay.

In Keld, Gatha's greatest creation had seized the country. His name was Kreig. He was the most powerful Keldon who ever lived, and he ruled as witch king. He made Gatha a lord of Keld with a voice in its government. Many Keldons took that as the last insult and rose against him, and Kreig crushed them easily. Under Kreig, Keld grew into a mighty nation.

It grew mighty enough to be noticed. Croag came to see what was happening there, and when he understood, he understood far more than Keld. Somebody on Dominaria was breeding people. He learned of the Bloodline project. Phyrexia began to strike at every place where it suspected the work was going on: Keld, Benalia, Yavimaya.
In 3863 AR Croag led a great attack on Keld in person. He wanted Gatha's research.

The Keldons began to lose. Gatha saw what he had done. His own stolen work was about to hand Phyrexia the secret of Urza's whole plan. He threw himself off a cliff, so that what he knew would die with him.

Kreig saw his friend fall. He charged Croag and wounded the Phyrexian lord so badly that Croag nearly died. Then the Witch King leapt from the same cliff, so that Phyrexia should not have his body either.

Keld had won the battle and lost both its rulers. The Keldons of the old blood took back their council and made war on Gatha's breed until it was wiped out. Phyrexia got into the ruins of Gatha's laboratory all the same.
Croag was a long time recovering. On Rath, Davvol took advantage of it. He proclaimed himself evincar and began to plan how to be rid of his master for good.

He was not quick enough. When Croag had healed, he destroyed the negator that Davvol sent against him. Then he clamped a device onto Davvol's skull that drew out everything the man knew about the Stronghold, and left him to die.

Rath went on growing. It needed a new evincar. The Bloodline project went on too, wounded and now known to the enemy. It had about three hundred years left to produce its hero, and so did Rath to reach its full size.

This chapter goes back to Ulgrotha, the small plane that was ruined in 3200 AR. A young planeswalker named Ravi rang an object called the Apocalypse Chime to end a war between planeswalkers. It killed almost everything on the plane and turned most of the land into a Dead Zone that drinks the life out of whatever walks on it. One corner survived, fed with mana through a rift from another world. The descendants of the survivors live there and call it the Homelands. Ravi shut herself in a magical coffin and then found that she could not get out.
Three people from other chapters come to Ulgrotha in this one.
Sengir was a baron's son on another world, Ravi's friend when both were children. His father's last spell turned him into a vampire.
Serra is the planeswalker who made a heaven of angels, healed Urza in it, and lost it to the Phyrexians who followed Urza there.
Taysir of Rabiah is the mighty planeswalker who loved Kristina of the Woods, lost her, and took the vengeful Ravidel as his pupil.

The dates in this chapter are the chronicle's. Other accounts place the same events up to three hundred years later, and nobody has reconciled them. The story comes from the background written for the card set Homelands and from a comic of the same name.

By 3420 AR the human survivors had been wandering the northern plains of the Homelands as nomads for two hundred years. They had split into families and forgotten where they came from. They had grown numerous, and they had begun to make war on one another.

Serra came to Ulgrotha in that year. She persuaded the nomads to make peace and to build a city. The city was named Onella, after the first abbot whom Serra chose to lead it. The country was named Aysen, after a group of stars that Serra said stood for harmony. Serra watched over Aysen as its protector, and its people came to worship her as a goddess. Aysen was governed by its abbey, with a great deal of paperwork, and its knights were the Paladins of Serra.

In the same years a colony of dwarves from another plane dug their way to Ulgrotha through an underground gate between worlds, looking for metals and gems. They founded a city beneath the mountains, called New Freedom. Above it, overlooking a salt marsh, they began to build a great castle of stone named Morning Light. Some of them built ships and sailed off to explore, leaving the rest to finish the castle.

Two planeswalkers then fought a duel in the swamps near the unfinished castle. One of them summoned a servant to fight for him, a vampire lord. That planeswalker lost and fled the plane, and he left his vampire behind.
It was Sengir. In the centuries since his boyhood he had become as ruthless as his father.

He had no means of leaving, so he decided to make the place his own. He took the dwarves' castle. He slaughtered everyone in it and raised them again as the walking dead. When the seafaring dwarves came home, they found their kin killed or turned. They knew every secret way into their own castle, and the Baron was still too strong for them. In one raid he captured Irini, the daughter of the dwarven king, made her a vampire, and bound her mind so that she was wholly loyal to him. He called her his daughter. Over the centuries he reshaped her to suit his taste, and undeath drove her mad, so that she spoke only in riddling verse and took a child's delight in cruelty.
The dwarves gave up. They swore an oath of vengeance, and they struck the knowledge of the gate between worlds out of their own history. They became wanderers of the sea.

The Baron found the gate under his throne room. Every servant he sent through it failed to return. He decided that he would go through one day with an army, and that he would build the army out of the peoples of the Homelands.
Searching the rest of the plane for anything useful, the Baron went deep into the Dead Zone. He found a ruined spire of black rock, and in it a sealed coffin. He opened it.

Inside was an ancient, withered, raving woman. She had lain awake in the dark for more than two hundred years. She remembered nothing of her life before the coffin. He did not know her, and she did not know him.

He saw at once that she had great magical power. He took her home to his castle and named her Grandmother Sengir. She calls him her grandson. She became his teacher of black magic and lost lore. The woman whose magic had been the magic of living things now works curses. Eggs spoil at the sound of her singing. She still has the Apocalypse Chime. In her madness she seems to have forgotten what it did, and she has been seen looking at it thoughtfully.
From her books came most of the dark magic that later corrupted the Homelands.

In 3560 AR another planeswalker came to Ulgrotha. Feroz was a scholar who travelled the Multiverse studying its peoples. He held an opinion that was rare among planeswalkers. He thought it wrong to summon living beings to fight one's battles.

Among the mountains of the Homelands lives a peaceful people of minotaurs, the Anaba, who honour the spirits of their ancestors. Feroz made a friend among them, a young minotaur named Sandruu, and taught him magic.
Feroz and Sandruu were fighting off a giant spider one day when a woman joined in. It was Serra. Feroz and Serra fell in love, and in time they married.

The Baron noticed that there were now two planeswalkers on his plane. He invited them to dinner at Castle Sengir. He told them courteously that he had regarded Ulgrotha as his home since the day he was stranded on it, and he warned them not to interfere with him. They ignored the warning. From then on Serra and Feroz worked to make the peoples of the Homelands strong enough to resist him. The Baron thought it wise to lie low for a while.
Feroz founded a school of magic on an island that floats in the sea, the Wizards' School, where he was called the First Master. In Onella a great abbey was raised in Serra's honour.
Under Feroz's teaching Sandruu's own spark woke, and the minotaur became a planeswalker. He went travelling. On Dominaria he met Kristina of the Woods, and the two became lovers.

Ravidel saw to it that Taysir found out. Ravidel had hated Kristina ever since she brought him back to life and left his friend the dragon dead. He took his master to a wood on Corondor and showed him Kristina walking with her new love. Taysir still loved her. He went after Sandruu in a fury and chased him home to Ulgrotha.

Taysir was among the most powerful planeswalkers who ever lived, and Sandruu had no chance. Taysir beat him and banished him to a plane so remote that it would take him a thousand years to find the way back. The duel wrecked the peace of the Anaba and destroyed the painted walls on which they kept their history.
Then Feroz arrived. He was the guardian of that world and Sandruu's friend. He fought Taysir, and he killed him. He split the great sorcerer's skull with a broadsword.

Taysir did not wholly die. Feroz himself saved the core of his being from destruction. Over the next two centuries the spirit-crafters of the Anaba and the spirits of their ancestors worked on that remnant, cooled its rage, and redeemed it. In the end Taysir was able to take a body again. He chose the body of a withered old man, as a sign of his repentance. He was a gentler person from then on.
Kristina never knew why Sandruu vanished. Ravidel had removed a rival, broken his master, and hurt the woman he hated, all with one word in the right ear.
Feroz and Serra had now seen what a single wandering planeswalker could do to their fragile world. They decided to shut all of them out.

They worked for nearly a year on their island. They studied the one stream of mana that keeps the Homelands alive, the one that flows in through the rift, and they studied a device of Serra's that could raise a wall of force. On the night when that stream ran strongest, Feroz cast the spell. It is called Feroz's Ban. It sealed Ulgrotha off from the rest of the Multiverse. No planeswalker could enter. None could even find the plane, or summon its creatures away to fight.

The Ban had a side effect. The mana flowing into the Homelands could no longer flow out, and it backed up. In the great forest of the Homelands there had always been a spirit of the wood, a mere presence. Fed on that surplus, it grew into a person with a body and a mind. She is called Autumn Willow, and she is the forest. She made faeries and other guardians to watch it, and she has a fondness for the human settlers of the forest town of An-Havva, among whom she sometimes walks in disguise. Trespassers who displease her are apt to be turned into lizards.

In Aysen there lived a street thief named Eron. On the Floating Island he met the head of the Wizards' School, a man of no principles, who offered him a bargain. If Eron stole a certain book of dark magic from Grandmother Sengir's library, the wizard would cast a spell for him.

Eron got into Castle Sengir, searched the library for hours, found the old woman asleep beside the book, and took it. He was a gambler. For his reward he asked for the last spell in the book, whatever it might be.
It made him immortal. He could not age, and any wound closed, though the scars and the aches stayed with him. The wizard was found out by the Baron and turned into a werewolf.

Eron tested his gift for a while by fighting whole squads of guards with a knife. Then he grew bored, walked into the goblin fortress in the Koskun Mountains, and announced that he was the King of the Goblins. They killed him on the spot. He got up. They killed him again. In the end they accepted him. He has been assassinated twenty-seven times since, and each time he comes back harder. He is called Eron the Relentless. He is a cruel king, and he also cares more than most for the future of the Homelands as a whole. He quietly sends food to the villages that the Baron keeps as his human herds in the swamp.

A young man of Aysen named Ihsan was troubled from boyhood by dreams in which he faced Baron Sengir in his castle. A fortune-teller told him that the dreams meant the Baron would be his doom. Ihsan took that as a calling. He became a Paladin of Serra and served for many years.

Then he went to Castle Sengir alone, knelt before the Baron, and begged to be made a vampire. It was a trick. Ihsan believed that the only way to destroy the Baron was to gain the Baron's own strength. He was ready to damn himself to do it.

The Baron had lived a long time, and he saw through it. He drank the paladin's blood. As Ihsan lay dying and pleading to be turned, the Baron spoke a spell that Grandmother had taught him. Ihsan died, and did not rise as a vampire. He rose as a shade, a helpless ghost, with his soul bound to the Baron's signet ring. Whoever holds the ring commands him. He has been the Baron's unwilling general ever since.
Ihsan wept and begged for a hundred days. What torments him most is that Aysen believes he went over to the enemy. His own order has sworn to destroy him as a traitor.

He had also taught the Baron something by accident. Fear of the vampires was what held Aysen together. The Baron stopped his raids. He waited to see whether Aysen, with no enemy to hate, would turn on itself. Within a few years it did. The stricter followers of Serra began to persecute a sect of fortune-tellers, and the Baron's agents fanned the quarrel.

parts.h: The end of the guardians (3780 AR)

blocks.p: In 3780 AR Feroz was studying a spirit of fire that was trapped in ice. The backed-up mana of his own Ban surged out of control during the experiment. Feroz was killed in front of his wife.

Serra was shattered. The Baron worked on her grief and her guilt, and she left Ulgrotha. She went to Dominaria, to a place called Sursi, and hid herself among a band of wandering refugees. There a planeswalker of dark magic, disguised as a thief, attacked her for the sake of a ring she wore. A man named Brother Angus drove the attacker off. Serra could easily have healed her own wounds. She no longer wished to live, and she let herself fade. With the last of her strength she blessed the land around Sursi, to make it a refuge for her followers against the dark. Brother Angus began to build a cathedral over her tomb.
So died the maker of the angels. Her church on Dominaria outlived her, and so did the angels.

Without Feroz the Ban began to come apart. The chronicle says that it had collapsed by 3800 AR. Ulgrotha lay open again. It had no guardians now. It had a goblin king who could not die, a forest that was a person, a school of wizards, a quarrelling church, and a patient vampire who had all the time in the world, with a mad old woman at his fireside who owned a chime.
This chapter tells how a mortal man killed Nicol Bolas.

Bolas is the oldest villain of this story: the Elder Dragon born on Dominaria twenty thousand years before the brothers Urza and Mishra, the planeswalker who killed his own twin brother Ugin twice, a master of the mind who holds that everything that exists ought to belong to him. About 3279 AR, fresh from killing Ugin on the plane of Tarkir, he seized a kingdom on Dominaria.

That kingdom was Madara, a group of islands west of the continent of Jamuraa. The largest island is also called Madara. On it there is a point where three kinds of mana meet: the mana of water, of swamp and of mountain. A planeswalker draws his magic from lands to which he has bound himself, and a place like that makes a strong anchor. Bolas killed the warrior queen who ruled there and took her throne. He built a shrine on the meeting point, the Imperial Shrine, and ruled from it as god-emperor.

Fifty years before Bolas came, a blind man had been set ashore on the same coast by a goddess. He was Toshiro Umezawa, the thief who ended the Kami War on the plane of Kamigawa. He founded a family in the swamps of Madara.
The story was told in three novels by Scott McGough, published between 2002 and 2003. They are followed here in the encyclopaedia's summaries.
A god-emperor does not govern. For more than three hundred years Bolas ruled Madara through three officers, and he took care that they balanced one another.

The first was the general of the kentsu. The kentsu was the imperial army. In 3607 AR its general was Marhault Elsdragon, a half-elven warrior and strategist of iron self-control, who was loyal to the emperor in everything and carried out any order gladly.

The second was the imperial assassin, who dealt with the emperor's enemies in secret. That was Ramses Overdark, a sorcerer of dark magic who lived in a keep in the northern swamps, guarded by a spirit of fire with which he had made a bargain. Lord Overdark was not loyal to anybody. He searched every order he was given for a loophole that would increase his own power. He meant to replace the other two officers with creatures of his own, and after them, if he could ever grow strong enough, the dragon.
The third was the imperial champion, who fought the emperor's battles in the open, by the rules of honour.

The champion was Tetsuo Umezawa, the son of the head of the Umezawa clan and a distant descendant of Toshiro. He was trained from boyhood in the fighting arts of his school: wrestling, the bow, the sword, and three kinds of magic. He was probably the most dangerous human being alive in his day. He was also brought up to a strict code of honour, and that was his difficulty.
At fifteen Tetsuo stood as his father's second in a formal duel. His father lost an eye, and by the rules the second had to take his place. It was the first time Tetsuo killed a man.

When the office of champion fell vacant he applied for it. He believed that a decent man in that post could protect the people of Madara, from foreign enemies and from the emperor's own temper. He had to fight the general of the day for it, and he won. The beaten general left the empire in disgrace and became a hermit.
Tetsuo gathered a small household of followers: his second, Tor Wauki, an archer; his armourer, Ayesha Tanaka; and a young healer, Kei Takahashi, who was Ayesha's pupil.
He and Ramses Overdark had been rivals since they were young.

One early adventure shows the kind of man he was. A fishing port named Sekana was being attacked by a nekoru, a creature that is part cat and part dragon. Her name was Wasitora. Tetsuo challenged her to a formal duel. A giant wurm blundered into the middle of it, and the cat-dragon helped him to kill it. Tetsuo decided that he need not kill her at all. He appointed her his deputy for the town. Wasitora became Sekana's guardian, and the townspeople waited on her in return.

parts.h: The first journey to the Edemis

blocks.p: Off the coast of Madara lie the Edemi Islands. The empire claimed them, and they rebelled every ten years or so. In 3607 AR two of them, Argenti and Kusho, broke away again. The leader of the rising was a noblewoman and famous archer, Lady Caleria.
Bolas sent his assassin to deal with it. Overdark saw a chance to do two things at once.

He sent his best killer, an insect-woman named Xira Arien, to murder the rebel leaders. Before she went, he had her lay one of her larvae in the body of Tetsuo's healer, Kei. That would draw Tetsuo to the islands in search of a cure. He also sent a monstrous servant, Lady Orca, to terrorise the islanders under the badge of Tetsuo's house. Either the rebels would kill the champion for crimes done in his name, or Overdark's creatures would kill champion and rebels together. He held one more weapon in reserve, an ancient machine that produced poisonous mechanical snakes.

Tetsuo defeated Orca, defeated Arien, and destroyed the machine. Lady Caleria saw whom she was dealing with and let him leave in peace. She even set one of her own people, Lord Magnus, to look for a cure for the boy. Tetsuo and Ayesha managed to kill the thing inside Kei. He kept the insect-like changes that it had made in him.
The islands stayed free.

Bolas was displeased with his assassin for failing and with his champion for having had a part in the failure. He gave the task to the army. General Elsdragon was to crush the islands, Overdark was to keep out of it, and Tetsuo and his household were to march with the kentsu as a punishment.

It was a brutal campaign. Tetsuo saw the emperor's soldiers do things that his honour could not excuse. On that march he made a friend. Kolo Meha was a mage of fire from the volcanic island of Bogardan, a cheerful, destructive man, who was travelling the world on a pilgrimage that his order required, to learn to work his magic in lands poorer in fire than his own. He was serving the kentsu as its expert in demolition. Long talks with Kolo Meha loosened Tetsuo's faith in the emperor further.

Overdark had not kept out of it. He had disobeyed a direct order. He had taken secret possession of the mind of the army's second in command, Marshal Jorgan Hage, so thoroughly that Hage himself did not know it. He had sent a shapeshifter named Halfdane to poison the mana of Kusho. He forged an imperial decree to bring Lady Orca back to the islands.

The kentsu won. Both islands were crushed. Then Orca turned on the army, and in the confusion Jorgan Hage cut off General Elsdragon's head and took his place. The emperor's army now belonged to the emperor's assassin.
Tetsuo's household was shattered in the same fighting. Ayesha was poisoned. Tor Wauki was badly wounded. Kei Takahashi was killed. Tetsuo suspected whose hand was behind it.
Bolas came to see Overdark. The dragon knew everything that his assassin had done.

He was not angry. He was impressed. He praised the man's ambition. The old arrangement of three officers, he said, had been out of date in any case. He abolished it and made Ramses Overdark imperial regent, the sole ruler of Madara under himself.

For Tetsuo that was the end. He had served a monster in the belief that he could shield the people from it, and the monster had just rewarded treachery, forgery and the murder of a loyal general. He renounced the title of champion and swore that he would have vengeance.

Tetsuo knew of a place where the emperor could not find him. It was the Meditation Realm, the still, strange plane of water and mist, where thought counts for more than flesh. Tetsuo knew the way there. He spent weeks in it, training, and he learned how the stuff of that place could be bent by a disciplined mind.

It was the very place where Nicol Bolas and Ugin had met as young dragons, and where Bolas had first killed his brother. For all that, the dragon did not understand its workings as well as his champion came to.

Overdark tried to flush him out. He sent a regiment of the kentsu to destroy Sekana. Wasitora and her kittens destroyed the regiment. Tetsuo saw that innocent people would keep dying for as long as he stayed hidden.

He settled his accounts in order. He hunted down Xira Arien for what she had done to Kei. He set Wasitora and her brood to guard his own house and servants. He sent Kolo Meha north to the regent's keep. Kolo, whom he had been training, fought the fire spirit that guarded it and beat it, and then destroyed the keep itself with a greater working of fire than he had ever attempted. That finished his pilgrimage. It also cut Ramses Overdark off from the main source of his magic.
Tetsuo went to the Imperial Shrine, where the regent and the emperor both were. The kentsu defended it. Tetsuo called a rain of burning stones out of the sky onto them.
Inside, he met Ramses Overdark alone. Overdark was a mighty sorcerer, but his keep was gone and half his strength with it. Tetsuo killed him and drew the dead man's power into himself.
Nicol Bolas was furious at the death of his regent.

Tetsuo did not stand and fight a dragon in the dragon's own hall. He let his spirit go out of the world, into the Meditation Realm. Bolas, in his rage, did what Tetsuo had counted on. He left his body where it lay in the shrine and went after the man in spirit.
Tetsuo had cast one more spell before he left. It was called the Meteor Hammer, and it was already falling.
It struck the Imperial Shrine and destroyed it utterly, with the body of Nicol Bolas inside.
Three things followed from that single blow, and each of them took something from the dragon.
His body was gone. A spirit with no body to return to cannot go back to the world it left. Bolas could not return to Dominaria, and he could not walk to any other plane either.
His anchor was gone. The shrine stood on the meeting point of the three kinds of mana, and it was the foothold that tied him to the magic of Dominaria. Without it nearly all his sorcery failed him.

And he was in the wrong place. In the Meditation Realm a dragon's size and strength mean nothing, because nothing there is made of flesh. What counts there is knowing how the place works. Tetsuo had studied it. Bolas, who had treated it for fifteen thousand years as a monument to himself, had not.

He was no longer a planeswalker in any way that mattered, nor a sorcerer, nor a dragon. He was an angry spirit in a realm of thought, facing a calm man who knew the ground. Tetsuo Umezawa fought him there and killed him.

Madara fell into chaos. Tetsuo was the only officer of the old order left alive. Nobles bought up regiments of the kentsu as private armies. The Edemi Islands demanded payment for what had been done to them. Peoples whom the empire had kept down rose up. Tetsuo was reunited with Kolo Meha, Tor Wauki and Ayesha Tanaka, and they persuaded him to take up the work of putting the country back together. How that ended was never told. In the present day Madara is ruled by the nekoru, the race of cat-dragons, and its humans live as their servants.
Bolas was dead. One trace of him was left.

Fifteen thousand years earlier, his fight with the Demonic Leviathan had torn a hole in time off the Madaran coast, at the place called the Talon Gates. Bolas had made that rift, and something of him was tied to it. When he died, a ghostly remnant of his life remained beside it, caught between the world and the Meditation Realm, unable to enter either. It stayed there for nine hundred years. An earlier chapter already showed, in the war on Ravnica at the end of the story, that this was not the last of him.

Many beings in this story set themselves against Nicol Bolas, his own brother among them. The one who killed him was a man with no spark, whose ancestor a goddess had thrown onto that beach as a punishment.

This chapter was the first one written, as a sample, and it stands far ahead of the rest. Almost ten thousand years of story lie between the fall of the Thran and the events told here, and those chapters are not written yet. Many of the people named below have not been introduced. This chapter is also shorter than the others, and it will be rewritten at full length when the story reaches it.

The elder dragon Nicol Bolas prepared the city-world of Ravnica long before he arrived there. One by one, Ravnica's guilds came under the control of planeswalkers whom Bolas believed he could steer: Ral Zarek rose in the Izzet League, Kaya took the Orzhov Syndicate, Vraska the Golgari Swarm, Domri Rade the Gruul Clans, and Dovin Baan climbed within the Azorius Senate.

Three of those five planeswalkers turned against Bolas. Ral, Kaya and Vraska saw what the dragon was, and tried to unite all ten guilds against him. They hoped to make the dragon Niv-Mizzet the new Living Guildpact, which would give Niv-Mizzet the power to face Bolas. The guild summit collapsed when Vraska killed the Azorius guildmaster Isperia. Trust between the guilds broke, Dovin took Isperia's seat, and Niv-Mizzet went to fight Bolas without the Guildpact's power and died. Vraska fled to Ixalan.

With the plan in ruins, Ral lit the Interplanar Beacon, a signal meant to call planeswalkers from across the Multiverse to Ravnica's defence. The planeswalkers came. Among them was the Gatewatch, a band of allied planeswalkers who were Bolas's chief opponents. Most of those who came did not know what was waiting for them.

The arrival of so many planeswalkers was exactly what Bolas wanted. Bolas switched on the Immortal Sun, an artifact that stops planeswalkers from leaving a plane, and no planeswalker on Ravnica could escape. On the Tenth District Plaza, Bolas and his servant Tezzeret raised Bolas's citadel and a towering statue of Bolas.

Tezzeret then opened the Planar Bridge to Amonkhet. The portal tore through the Embassy of the Guildpact, broke Ravnica's leylines and stripped Jace of the Living Guildpact's power. Through the portal marched the Dreadhorde, Bolas's army of undead warriors called Eternals. The planeswalker Liliana Vess led the Dreadhorde against her will, because a demonic contract bound her to obey Bolas. The Eternals killed whoever they found, to draw the planeswalkers out.

The Boros Legion and House Dimir declared against Bolas. Ral brought the Izzet and talked the Simic into joining; Kaya won the grudging support of the Orzhov. Under Aurelia and Feather, with Gideon beside them and the flying fortress Parhelion II in the lead, the Boros drove the invaders back.

Nissa woke Vitu-Ghazi, the great tree that was the Selesnya guildhall, and walked it into battle as a colossal elemental. The walking tree pushed the Dreadhorde back and pulled down Bolas's statue, and for a moment the city believed it could win.
Bolas answered by bringing the God-Eternals through the portal: the gods of Amonkhet, dead and remade as his weapons. The God-Eternals tore Vitu-Ghazi apart, and the Boros fell back.

Then Bolas cast the Elderspell. From that moment, every Eternal that laid hands on a planeswalker ripped out that planeswalker's spark and sent it to Bolas. A planeswalker whose spark is torn out in that way dies. Domri Rade, who had sworn himself to Bolas, was the first to die.

The trapped planeswalkers and Ravnica's leaders met to plan, and Nissa rejoined the Gatewatch there. On the advice of Jace Beleren, one of the leaders of the Gatewatch, the defenders split into teams.

Gideon, Aurelia, Angrath and Huatli led the armies against the God-Eternal Rhonas, and Gideon killed Rhonas with a sword called the Blackblade. Ajani and others rescued civilians. Ral shut down the Beacon so that no more planeswalkers would be lured in. Chandra, Saheeli, Lavinia and Lazav went for the Immortal Sun, which Dovin guarded; Lazav disguised himself as Chandra to act as a decoy, while the real Chandra switched the Immortal Sun off. Dovin was blinded in the fight and fled the plane.

Karn, Ob Nixilis, Dack Fayden and Samut crossed the Planar Bridge to Amonkhet and beat Tezzeret, which closed the portal. On Amonkhet the god Hazoret gave the four planeswalkers her spear to use against Bolas. Jace, Jaya, Teferi and Vivien tried to kill Liliana and nearly succeeded, but Bolas stepped in to save Liliana, his general.

Kaya, with the newly sparked Teyo and the Gateless girl Araithia, went to the guilds that had stayed out: Selesnya, Gruul, Golgari and Rakdos. With help from Vraska, who had returned to Ravnica, Kaya's team persuaded those four guilds to join the fight. After Dovin's defeat, Lavinia brought the Azorius in as well. With the Immortal Sun off, many planeswalkers left at once. A few stayed.

All ten guilds now stood together, and the ritual that had failed before was performed. The ritual mended the leylines and brought Niv-Mizzet back from death as the Living Guildpact. Niv-Mizzet burned the God-Eternal Kefnet to nothing, and the effort left Niv-Mizzet unconscious.

For the last assault Gideon had Chandra switch the Immortal Sun on again, this time to keep Bolas from escaping. Planeswalkers and Ravnican soldiers stormed the citadel. Dack Fayden died in the fighting, his spark taken.

Gideon flew at Bolas on a pegasus. The God-Eternal Oketra shot the pegasus out from under him with an arrow. Liliana was controlling Oketra, and Liliana had deliberately aimed at the pegasus and not at Gideon. The demon Rakdos caught the falling Gideon and carried him within reach of Bolas. Bolas swatted Rakdos aside. Gideon leapt from the demon and struck Bolas in the face with the Blackblade, and the sword shattered. Bolas had enchanted the Blackblade thousands of years earlier, so that it could never again harm an elder dragon.

Then Liliana turned against Bolas. Bolas cancelled Liliana's contract, and the breaking of the contract began to destroy her body. Gideon used his own magic to transfer the price of Liliana's broken contract onto himself. Gideon died in Liliana's place.

Liliana, now free, released the God-Eternals Oketra and Bontu from her control, and the two God-Eternals attacked Bolas of their own will. As Bolas turned to meet them, Niv-Mizzet drove Hazoret's spear into Bolas's back. Bolas still managed to strike Niv-Mizzet down and to destroy Oketra. But Bontu bit Bolas, and through the bite she drew out every spark Bolas had stolen, and Bolas's own spark with them. Bontu could not hold that much power, and it destroyed her.

Ugin, the Spirit Dragon, came for his brother's body. Ugin carried Bolas to the Meditation Realm, so that Bolas could not come back to life on Ravnica. At Ugin's request, Jace created an illusion of Bolas's corpse crumbling to dust, so that no one would try to follow. Ravnica celebrated, and Kaya took the oath of the Gatewatch.

The guilds did not forget who had served Bolas first. Niv-Mizzet and the guild leaders ordered Ral, Kaya and Vraska to atone by hunting down the dragon's other agents: Ral was to find Tezzeret, Vraska to track Dovin, and Kaya was sent to kill Liliana.

Months later Bolas woke in the Meditation Realm without power: no magic, no way to walk the planes. Ugin told Bolas that he, Ugin, had planned Bolas's defeat together with Niv-Mizzet and the planeswalker Sarkhan. Ugin had also taken away Bolas's names, so that no one could ever summon Bolas again. Ugin had merged his own being with the Meditation Realm and sealed the realm shut. Neither brother can leave, and Ugin will keep watch there until Bolas dies.
